page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with cached small-block read operations ranking in the bottom 10% at 136.13 GB/sec, and uncached large-block read and write speeds both ranking in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark memory scores and database operations rank in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile, this server represents a low-resource entry point within the compute-optimized family, offering a qualitative balance of dedicated AMD EPYC execution at a minimal resource footprint. It is best suited for single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, or lightweight web serving where multi-core scaling and high memory throughput are not critical. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or parallelized workloads.
